store.name: Fellreach
store.tagline: Gear for the long way round.
store.voice: Quiet, plain and outdoors: short sentences that start from the place and the weather, then the gear. Specific about fabric, weight and fit; honest about limits. Calm, a little dry, never macho, no hype words, no exclamation marks. US spelling.
store.story: Fellreach started in 2017 in a former feed store in a small mountain town on the dry side of the Cascades. A ski patroller and a sailmaker wanted shells, wool and packs that could take a decade of weather and still be fixed at a bench. They test everything on the ridges above town and on the outer coast, keep a small range, and repair what they sell, for life.

policies.refund: Return anything unworn, with its tags, within 60 days of delivery for a full refund to the original payment method. If something fails in use because of how we made it, we repair it, replace it or refund it, for as long as you own it. Returns in the US are free with the label in your order email; returns from Canada are at your cost. Start a return or a claim at hello@fellreach.example with your order number.
policies.shipping: Orders ship from our warehouse in Twisp, Washington, within two business days. Standard shipping is $9 to the US and Canada and free on orders over $150. US orders usually arrive in 3 to 6 business days, Canadian orders in 5 to 10. Canadian orders may owe duties and taxes on delivery. You get a tracking link by email when your parcel leaves.
policies.privacy: We keep what we need to run the shop: your name, email, shipping address, order history and, if you send us gear, your repair records. Payments are handled by our payment provider; we never see or store your card number. We never sell your data. Our newsletter is opt-in and every email has an unsubscribe link. To see or delete what we hold about you, write to hello@fellreach.example.
policies.terms: Prices are in US dollars, before taxes and duties. Colors can look a little different on screen than outdoors. We may cancel an order if a price was listed in error, and we refund it in full if we do. Outdoor gear helps, but it does not replace judgment: check the forecast and know your route. These terms are governed by the laws of the State of Washington.

art_direction: Fellreach, a quiet outdoor apparel and gear brand whose shop is led by large photographs. Realistic photography only, never illustration or 3D. LIGHT AND MOOD: natural light only, overcast, first light or dusk; moody mountain ridges, misty valleys, larch forests, alpine lakes and a wild, foggy northern coast with dark rocks and pebble beaches; calm, wide and still, with generous empty sky or water. PALETTE: muted earth tones (slate gray, moss, peat brown, stone, sand, deep spruce green, fog white) with one warm ochre accent; deep shadows that sit well on a near-black green page; slightly desaturated, fine film grain, 35mm or 50mm lens. PEOPLE: invented adults seen from behind, far away or small in the landscape, never a recognizable face, never posing for the camera. PRODUCT SHOTS: the item alone, centered with space around it in a tall frame, on weathered dark granite, gray driftwood or a rough slate wall with a wooden peg, soft side light, true-to-life matte fabrics and visible texture, or worn outdoors in the landscape. ALWAYS AVOID: any text, letters, numbers, logos, brand marks, labels, tags or patches with marks, readable signs, watermarks; bright saturated colors; studio seamless backdrops; selfies.

products.name: Headwall 3L Shell Jacket
products.description_html:
Our most-used shell: three layers, fully taped and cut to move, for days when the forecast changes its mind three times before lunch.

Features

  • Helmet-compatible hood with a laminated brim and one-hand adjusters
  • Two-way front zip and long pit zips for dumping heat on the climb
  • Two chest pockets that clear a pack hip belt and a harness
  • Articulated sleeves that stay put at the wrist when you reach

Materials

Three-layer recycled nylon face with a waterproof, breathable membrane (20,000 mm) and a PFC-free water-repellent finish. 15.2 oz in a men's medium.

Fit

Regular fit with room for a fleece and a light insulated layer underneath. Hem drops a little at the back.

Care

Machine wash warm with a technical wash, close every zip first. Tumble dry low to refresh the water-repellent finish. Repairs for life at our workshop.

images.alt: Headwall 3L Shell Jacket in slate, laid flat on dark granite

Fit

Care

Machine wash warm, tumble dry low. Store it unpacked at home so the coating lasts.

products.name: Cairn Down Jacket
products.description_html:
The jacket for the cold half of the day: camp at dusk, belays in the wind, the first hour before the sun clears the ridge.

Features

  • Box-wall baffles across the core, so no cold spots at the seams
  • Insulated hood that fits over a beanie
  • Two fleece-lined hand pockets and one inside stash pocket
  • Packs into its own stuff sack, included

Materials

800-fill traceable goose down under a 20-denier recycled nylon shell with a water-repellent finish. 14 oz of jacket, 5.6 oz of down in a medium.

Fit

Regular fit, slightly longer at the back. Wear it over everything, or under a shell when the weather turns wet.

Care

Machine wash cold on a gentle cycle with a down wash. Tumble dry low with two clean tennis balls until fully dry; it takes a while.

pages.title: Our story
pages.content_html:
Fellreach started in 2017 in a former feed store at the edge of a small town on the dry side of the Cascades. One of us patrolled the ski hill above town; the other had spent fifteen years making and mending sails on the coast. We both owned too many jackets that leaked by their third winter and could not be fixed.

A small range, worn hard

We make about two dozen things: shells, insulation, wool, trail pants and packs. Every piece is worn for a full year on the ridges above town and on the outer coast before it goes on sale, and most of them change in that year. When something works, we keep making it, in the same pattern, for as long as we can.

Made to be mended

Our workshop sits behind the shop. Send us anything we make, at any age, and we will patch it, replace a zip, re-tape a seam or re-wax the canvas at cost. Last year we fixed 1,900 pieces. The best gear is the gear you already own.

Materials we can stand behind

Recycled nylon and polyester, merino from mulesing-free farms, traceable down and waxed organic cotton, with PFC-free water repellents throughout. We work with five factories, in Portugal, Poland and Vietnam, and we visit each of them every year.

Come by

The shop and workshop are open Thursday to Monday. Bring muddy boots and questions about trails; we have both opinions and maps.

pages.title: Contact
pages.content_html:
Write to us at hello@fellreach.example or call (509) 555-0162. A real person answers, usually the same day.

Shop and workshop

47 Larkspur Lane, Twisp, WA 98856

Thursday to Monday, 9 am to 5 pm. Closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays, when we are out testing.

Repairs

Drop gear off at the workshop counter or post it to the address above with a note: your name, your email and what needs doing. See repairs for how it works.

Wholesale and press

Use the same email with "Wholesale" or "Press" in the subject line.

pages.title: Shipping & returns
pages.content_html:
Shipping

Orders ship from Twisp, Washington, within two business days. Standard shipping is $9 to the US and Canada, and free on orders over $150.

  • United States: usually 3 to 6 business days
  • Canada: usually 5 to 10 business days; duties and taxes may be due on delivery

You will get a tracking link by email as soon as your parcel leaves.

Returns

Return anything unworn, with its tags, within 60 days of delivery for a full refund. US returns are free with the prepaid label in your order email; Canadian returns are at your cost. Refunds go back to the original payment method within five business days of the parcel reaching us.

Exchanges

The quickest way to change a size or color is to return the first piece and place a new order, so the one you want does not sell out while the parcel travels.

If something fails

If a seam lets go or a zip breaks because of how we made it, we will repair, replace or refund it, however old it is. Write to hello@fellreach.example with a photo and your order number, if you still have it.

pages.title: Size guide
pages.content_html:
Measure over a base layer, with the tape snug but not tight. Between sizes, take the larger for jackets and the smaller for base layers.

Tops and jackets

  • XS: chest 33 to 35 in
  • S: chest 35 to 37 in
  • M: chest 38 to 40 in
  • L: chest 41 to 43 in
  • XL: chest 44 to 46 in
  • XXL: chest 47 to 49 in

Trail pants

Pants are sized by waist in inches, with a 32 in inseam. We hem them free of charge at the workshop: send them back with a note of the length you want.

Fits

  • Next to skin: base layers, close without squeezing
  • Trim: active layers that sit close for climbing and skiing
  • Regular: room for a fleece and a light puffy underneath
  • Relaxed: room for a thick sweater

Packs

Measure your torso from the bone at the base of your neck to the top of your hip bones. The Long Valley comes in S/M (15 to 18 in) and M/L (18 to 21 in); the Traverse fits 16 to 20 in.

pages.title: Repairs for life
pages.content_html:
We repair everything we make, for as long as you own it. Wear and tear is fixed at cost; anything that fails because of how we made it is fixed free.

What we fix

  • Tears and holes in shells, fleece and packs, with patches matched as closely as we can
  • Broken zips and sliders
  • Lifting seam tape
  • Worn cuffs, hems and hip belt buckles
  • Waxed canvas, re-waxed
  • Wool, darned by hand

What it costs

  • Patch: from $15
  • Zip slider: $12; full zip: from $45
  • Re-taping a seam: from $25
  • Re-waxing a jacket or bag: $40

How to send it

Wash the piece, put a note inside with your name, email and what needs doing, and post it to 47 Larkspur Lane, Twisp, WA 98856. We email a quote before we start. Most repairs take two to three weeks, longer in early winter.

posts.title: Three days on the high route
posts.content_html:
We left the trailhead at five, in the dark, with three days of food and a forecast that said "mostly clear." It was, for about six hours.

Day one: up and over

The first pass came at noon, after four thousand feet of switchbacks through larch that were just starting to turn. We ate lunch on a slab above a lake the color of slate and watched cloud come up the valley behind us.

Day two: inside the cloud

We walked most of the second day in fog so thick we navigated cairn to cairn. The Headwall shells earned their keep: eight hours of wind-driven drizzle, hoods up, pit zips open on the climbs. Nobody was cold, and nobody was wet from the inside, which is the part that matters.

Day three: the clearing

It broke at dawn on the third morning. We sat in our down jackets with coffee in enamel mugs and watched the cloud sink into the valleys until only the peaks were left. Then we walked down, slowly, the long way round.

What we carried

  • Long Valley 45L Pack
  • Headwall 3L Shell Jacket and Cairn Down Jacket
  • Merino 200 Crew, worn three days running
  • Switchback Trail Pant

image.alt: Two hikers on a ridge above a sea of cloud at dawn

posts.title: A wet week on the outer coast
posts.content_html:
Every October we take the new season's samples to the outer coast for a week. It rains there two days out of three, the wind does not stop, and sand gets into everything. It is the best test we know.

Walking the headlands

Most days we walked ten or twelve miles: over headlands on muddy trails, down rope ladders to the beaches, across creek mouths at low water. The Squall jacket lived in a hip pack and came out every hour.

What failed

A zip slider on a sample pack corroded in four days of salt spray. We have changed the slider for the production run, and we will keep testing it next year.

What we kept

The Wool Camp Blanket by the evening fire, the Shieling crew under everything, and a waxed cap that has now been to the coast five years running. Some things you do not need to change.

image.prompt: A foggy wild northern beach with dark sea stacks and drifted logs, an invented person in a dark rain jacket with the hood up walking away along the wet sand, small in the frame, gray sea and heavy rain clouds, reflections on the wet sand.
image.alt: A walker in a rain jacket on a foggy beach among sea stacks

posts.title: First snow at the hut
posts.content_html:
There is a small wooden hut four hours above town that we try to reach every year on the weekend of the first real snow. This year it came early, on the first of November.

The walk in

The trail was dry for the first two hours and white for the last two. The larches still held their gold, which made the whole valley look lit from inside. We wore grid fleece and shells on the climb and stopped every half hour to shake the snow off the branches above us, for no good reason.

The night

The hut stove takes an hour to warm the room. We spent it in the Bothy fleece and wool beanies, melting snow for tea and drying gloves on a string across the ceiling.

The morning

Eight inches of new snow, a blue sky and not a single track in the valley. We walked out on the same trail and it felt like a different place.
